text: A young engineer is sawing gaps into a brand new railroad. On purpose.
Two companies are racing to build a line along the same desert canyon. First to finish wins every customer.
His boss finds a gap between every rail, as wide as a finger.
Are you trying to ruin me?
The rival lays its rails tight together, smooth as glass. And wins the race.
Their trains whisper along the cliffs. His rattle over every single gap.
People nickname his line the Rattler. And they all ride the quiet one.
Then summer arrives. And his gaps begin to shrink.
In spring, a coin fits inside. By July, not even a playing card.
Ha! Even the steel is fixing your mistake.
But across the canyon, the smooth rails start to creak. Steel grows in the heat. And theirs has nowhere to go.
On the hottest day of the year, his gaps close. Rail meets rail. A perfect fit.
On the other side, the track kicks sideways like a snake. Just as a train comes around the bend.
The driver slams the brakes, and stops a few feet short.
By autumn, the rival is sawing gaps into every mile.
And that clickety-clack on old railroads? That is the sound of room to grow.
